title: Introduction to Learner-First Systemic Education
subtitle: How to design instruction that actually shifts mental models
description: An introduction to the Learner-First Systemic Education framework — the ISRD approach to instructional design for complex domains. Covers attractor theory applied to learning, the seven-phase module structure, AI tutoring architecture, and simulation as an epistemological tool. Includes hands-on design exercises using ISRD simulation tools.

modules_preview.title: The Attractor Problem in Learning
modules_preview.desc: Why traditional instruction fails complex domains and what attractor theory reveals about persistent misconceptions.

modules_preview.title: Phase 1–2: Surfacing and Perturbation
modules_preview.desc: How to reveal the learner's current mental model and introduce productive instability.

modules_preview.title: Phase 3–4: Exposition and Simulation
modules_preview.desc: Minimal structural exposition followed by direct simulation-based exploration.

modules_preview.title: Phase 5: AI-Facilitated Reflection
modules_preview.desc: Designing the pedagogical context for AI Socratic dialogue — goals, misconception library, adaptive scaffolding.

modules_preview.title: Phase 6–7: Transfer and Integration
modules_preview.desc: Cross-domain transfer challenges and explicit course graph navigation.

modules_preview.title: Course as Feedback System
modules_preview.desc: Designing the dependency network connecting course modules and modeling the learner's attractor trajectory.

modules_preview.title: Applied Design Project
modules_preview.desc: Design a complete Learner-First Systemic Education module for a complex domain of your choice.

title: Introduction to Systems Science
subtitle: The four eras of systems thinking and why they matter now
description: A ground-up introduction to systems science — from General Systems Theory through cybernetics, complexity science, and the AI era. Each era is explored through interactive simulations and AI-facilitated reflection. Includes the Feedback Loops, Lorenz Attractor, and Emergence simulations.

title: Post-Viral Illness as a Complex System
subtitle: Understanding ME/CFS and chronic conditions through attractor dynamics
description: A systems-based course for clinicians, patients, and researchers working with post-viral and treatment-resistant conditions. Uses the ME/CFS Population Outbreak Simulator and brainstem ANS model as learning instruments. Applies Learner-First Systemic Education design throughout.
